tasks.answer: The incident is consumption-side, not production-side. Messages ARE arriving at the topic (order-service stayed steady at ~230 req/s throughout, healthy), but settlement-service's consumer cannot process them: starting 07:42:14Z it fails to deserialize "OrderExecuted ... missing required field 'qty' (schema v1 expected, header says v2)" at offset orders-3@8841207, then the partition is blocked by a poison-message retry loop. Alternative origin within the same mechanism is not formally separated: 'unable to read data at a schema id computed at startup' (stale/registered-schema-ceiling problem — consumer or registry compatibility fault) would produce the identical error signature but a different fix (fix/re-point the consumer scheme, not roll back the producer). Lag onset is only bracketed at 8-minute resolution (between 07:32Z and 07:40Z) [F7], so the producer change at 07:40Z is co-bucketed with rather than strictly preceding the first lag rise; strict temporal precedence is established only for the 07:42:14Z parse error. It is nonetheless the right rejection — the affirmative parse error on a specific offset with the consumer actively polling and nacking is incompatible with a lost assignment — and this residual gap is a reason for the confidence cap, not for another round.
